hints: In right $\triangle BPC$, evaluate $\tan(\angle ABC) = \frac{9}{3} = 3$ and find the angle in radians to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
In the right-angled triangle $\triangle APC$, use the Pythagorean theorem to calculate $AP$:
$$AP = \sqrt{AC^2 - CP^2} = \sqrt{15^2 - 9^2} = \sqrt{225 - 81} = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}$$

Find the length of $BP$ along the side $AB = 15\text{ cm}$:
$$BP = AB - AP = 15 - 12 = 3\text{ cm}$$

In the right-angled triangle $\triangle BPC$, calculate $\angle ABC$:
$$\tan(\angle ABC) = \frac{CP}{BP} = \frac{9}{3} = 3$$
$$\angle ABC = \tan^{-1}(3) \approx 1.24904 \approx 1.25\text{ radians} \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

hints: Calculate the area of sector $BCQ = \frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{90})^2(\tan^{-1}3) = 45(1.24904) \approx 56.21\text{ cm}^2$.
Calculate the area of right $\triangle BPC = \frac{1}{2}(3)(9) = 13.5\text{ cm}^2$.
Subtract the triangle area from the sector area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the radius $BC$ of the circle centred at $B$:
$$BC = \sqrt{BP^2 + CP^2} = \sqrt{3^2 + 9^2} = \sqrt{9 + 81} = \sqrt{90}\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the area of sector $BCQ$ with radius $\sqrt{90}$ and angle $\angle ABC = 1.24904\text{ radians}$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } BCQ) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(90)(1.24904) \approx 56.207\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $\triangle BPC$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle BPC) = \frac{1}{2} \times BP \times CP = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 9 = 13.5\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the triangle area from the sector area to find the shaded area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 56.207 - 13.5 = 42.707 \approx 42.7\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$
